events.label: Sam steps into Quantum Accelerator
events.description: Scientist Sam Beckett steps into his own unfinished time-travel machine, the Quantum Leap Accelerator, and vanishes from his present without any way to steer it.

events.label: First leap into host body; mirror shock
events.description: Sam wakes up in 1956 as a test pilot, someone else entirely - and when he looks in a mirror he sees a stranger's face staring back at him, not his own.

events.label: Hologram Al and Ziggy guide the mission
events.description: Sam's best friend Al appears as a hologram only Sam can see, with the project's supercomputer Ziggy feeding them guesses about why Sam is there and how to help.

events.label: Put right what once went wrong for the host
events.description: Whatever life Sam lands in, his job is the same: put right what once went wrong for the person he has become, then move on.

events.label: Leap out after success; next host
events.description: Once the wrong is put right, Sam leaps out in a flash of light - straight into the next stranger's life, never knowing where or when he'll land.

events.label: Years of leaps across mid-century America
events.description: Year after year, Sam drifts through mid-century America - a rodeo rider, a secretary, a black man in the segregated South - quietly fixing broken lives wherever he lands.

events.label: Finale Mirror Image: leap into a bar that is himself/God?
events.description: In the final episode Sam walks into a dingy bar on the night he was born, where every soul inside looks like someone he has met on his journeys - including a bartender who may be more than a bartender, and who may be himself.

events.label: Sam chooses to continue leaping to help others
events.description: Told he could stop and go home if he wished, Sam instead chooses to keep leaping - one more stranger's life to set right, and then another.

events.label: Al's personal timeline improved (Beth waits)
events.description: Sam's very last leap changes Al's own past: he tells Al's wife Beth that her husband is coming home, so she waits for him all those years instead of moving on.

events.label: Title card: Sam Beckett never returned home
events.description: The closing title card delivers the show's bittersweet verdict: Dr Sam Beckett never returned home.

events.label: Leaping framed as string/God/conscience mechanism
events.description: The show wraps its time-hopping in talk of string theory, and leaves room for stranger answers - that Sam's leaps might be guided by God, fate, or his own conscience.

events.label: Host lives corrected life after Sam leaps out
events.description: When Sam leaps away, the person he was inhabiting wakes up in their own body again - living on with a life Sam has quietly put back on track.

events.label: Project observes from imaging chamber
events.description: Back home, the team at Project Quantum Leap watch Sam's journey through the Imaging Chamber, guessing at history's plans since they can't always see what he faces.

events.label: Sam leaps into another life
events.description: Sam Beckett steps out of his own time and wakes in the body of another person, somewhere in the past.

events.label: Al hologram guidance
events.description: Only Sam can see Al, his rakish hologram sidekick, who pops in with advice, gadgets from the future and a car he shouldn't have.

events.label: Ziggy probability calculations
events.description: The project's snarky supercomputer Ziggy crunches the odds, telling Sam and Al what probably went wrong and what Sam probably needs to fix.

events.label: Put right what once went wrong
events.description: Each leap hands Sam a simple, human mission: find the moment someone's life went wrong and set it right before he can move on.

events.label: Leap out when mirror shows next
events.description: When the job is done, Sam vanishes in blue light and lands in someone new - and the person he helped never quite remembers him.

events.label: Never quite home arc
events.description: Across five seasons Sam keeps hoping the next leap will take him home, but the road never bends back to his own front door.

events.label: Evil leaper arcs
events.description: Lurking through the later series is the shadow of an evil leaper - another traveller, and an Al-like guide, who leap through time making things worse.

events.label: Series finale revelations
events.description: The final episode reveals the bar, the bartender and the stakes of Sam's journey - and ends with his choice to leap on, never going home.

ruleEffects.effect: Correcting host history ripples outcomes (Al's marriage etc.)
Sam's own return home is withheld — leap destiny closed against homecoming

outcome.summary: Sam never returns; continues leaping by choice; Al's life improved; theological Mirror Image coda.
